subject: VitalHealth — eastus2 errstorm & cross-region routing playbook
messages:
From: Alejandra Morales <alejandra@vitalhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: VitalHealth Ops <ops@vitalhealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-12 09:14 -0400
Subject: Production: sudden 5xx + token backlog in eastus2

David —

We started seeing a large number of 502/504s around 08:50 ET and our user-visible error rate spiked above 8% for the next 25 minutes. Latency for inference requests jumped from ~120ms p95 to >1.2s. Throughput is throttling and requests are being retried aggressively from our side which is amplifying the issue.

We are on Dedicated capacity (commit: DEAL-7843) pinned to eastus2. Can you confirm whether this is an AZ-level problem or if there's a routing/fabric issue? We need an immediate mitigation plan — either a controlled cross-region steer or a fallback model variant. This is impacting our patient-facing workflows.

Attached: a sample log extract and a short chart from our SLO dashboard.

—Alejandra
Alejandra Morales
Head of Site Reliability, VitalHealth
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alejandra Morales <alejandra@vitalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12 09:21 -0400
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx + token backlog in eastus2

Alejandra —

Thanks for the heads up and the attachment. We're looking at the cluster now. First pass from infra shows a burst of KV-cache evictions followed by worker restarts in eastus2-az1 which is consistent with a memory-pressure cascade; that would explain the token backlog and elevated latencies.

Immediate actions we are taking (ETA):
- Initiating an emergency traffic redistribution to eastus3 (non-primary) — engineering lead: Marissa; ETA 12m
- Bringing up a quantized fallback that reduces memory per replica for this workload — engineering lead: Sean; ETA 22m
- Enabling temporary 429 fast-fail policy on retrying clients to stop amplification (we will coordinate with your client-side team) — ETA 8m

We'll loop you in with an exec summary and share the runbook link shortly. Apologies for the disruption; we'll keep the channel updated every 15 minutes.

—David
David Kim
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: runbook-cross-region-steer-v1.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12 09:28 -0400
Subject: eastus2 worker restarts — plan and asks

Team —

Observed: between 08:48–09:05 ET eastus2-az1 showed a sustained GC/oom pattern on several workers serving VitalHealth. Telemetry indicates KV cache eviction rates spiked ~3.7x baseline and the worker autoscaler lagged while new heavier-quantized replicas initialized.

Actions taken so far:
- Traffic peel started to eastus3 at 09:23 ET (low-volume ramp). Current cross-region ratio: eastus2:eastus3 = 85:15 (we're tuning).
- Warmed quantized variant q4_0-medium on 4 nodes in eastus3.
- Temporarily adjusted autoscale thresholds on the VitalHealth route to be more aggressive.

Asks for CS/Customer:
- Ask VitalHealth to momentarily reduce client-side retry concurrency; ops contact looped.
- Permission to open a short read-only access to selected logs for VitalHealth SREs (I will share a presigned link).

I'll keep the ramp controlled — we want to avoid cascading cold-starts. If error rate doesn't drop under 2% within 35 minutes we'll request exec-level credit/comp consideration for the incident.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alejandra Morales <alejandra@vitalhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: VitalHealth Ops <ops@vitalhealth.com>, Luke Chen <luke.chen@vitalhealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-12 10:02 -0400
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx + token backlog in eastus2

David / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick actions. We're dialing back client retry concurrency and have paused a subset of background jobs to reduce load. Please go ahead with the cross-region ramp and share the presigned logs. Also tagging Luke who will coordinate SSO access if needed.

Two asks from our side:
1) ETA for full (safe) cutover if eastus2 cannot stabilize (our risk team needs timing for swap).
2) Any expected change in model output quality with the quantized fallback (q4_0-medium) — our clinicians need to know if there will be degraded responses.

—Alejandra
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alejandra Morales <alejandra@vitalhealth.com>, VitalHealth Ops <ops@vitalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12 15:02 -0400
Subject: Post-mortem short update & next steps — eastus2 incident (VitalHealth)

Alejandra / Luke / Ops —

Summary (what happened):
- Root cause: an atypical memory leak in a user-specific preprocessing path (identified in VitalHealth client graph) caused excessive KV-cache churn in eastus2-az1 leading to worker restarts and token eviction amplification.
- Impact: peak 5xx = 9.4% (09:00–09:18 ET); p95 latency peaked to ~1.3s; throughput loss ~28% for 20m.

What we did (immediate mitigation):
- Controlled ramp of traffic to eastus3 and warmed q4_0-medium replicas reduced 5xx to <1.2% by 09:45 ET.
- Applied routing guardrails to prevent cascade (retry fast-fail + client-side concurrency guidance).
- Shared pre-signed logs and extracted sample stack traces (link below).

Outstanding items / next steps:
1) Joint RCA session scheduled: 2027-09-13 11:00 ET (includes engineering and your SREs) — link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/vitalhealth/incidents/2027-09-12
2) We'll run a targeted quality regression eval between the primary and quantized fallback with your clinical test set; Sean leading, ETA 48h.
3) Suggest a short runbook change: pin KV cache soft-limits for dedicated routes on customer-owned Dedicated accounts — Marissa to propose wording.
4) Compensation ask process: if VitalHealth prefers, I will escalate to sales leadership for one-time credit; we discussed possible credit in earlier comms.

Attached: s3 presigned log archive, a short incident timeline snapshot, and the runbook excerpt.

Appreciate the partnership and the rapid coordination. We'll follow up after the RCA.

—David
David Kim
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
